claim: The episode frames KV cache behavior as a practical context engineering concern for agent speed and cost.
Changing the available tool set during a conversation can break the stable prompt prefix and cause a cache miss.
Stable prompt construction can improve throughput, but the speakers say builders need measurements to know whether caching is working.
Few shot examples should be selected narrowly and kept to the minimum needed for the task.
Specific agents can receive a selected slice of context instead of the full conversation.
Token level constraints can still allow unwanted continuations because the model acts on token prefixes rather than human concepts.
